newsitem.title: MEXICO: BOXING-WBC DECLARES WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE VACANT.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-WBC DECLARES WORLD HEAVYWEIGHT TITLE VACANT.

text.p: The World Boxing Council (WBC) said on Tuesday that Mike Tyson relinquished its heavyweight championship.
The WBC declared the heavyweight title vacant and said it would hold a public purse bid for a title fight between Lennox Lewis of Britain and Oliver McCall of the United States.

"The World Boxing Council has taken a voting by its board of governors in order to strip the world heavyweight champion, Mike Tyson, of his title," the Mexico City-based WBC said in an English-language statement.
The purse offer will take place at WBC headquarters in Mexico City on Thursday, the statement said.
the WBC move followed an order by a New Jersey court earlier this year that Tyson had to fight Lewis before facing World Boxing Association (WBA) champion Bruce Seldon.
But Tyson's promoter, Don King, paid Lewis $4 million to step aside and agree that Tyson's WBC belt would not be on the line against Seldon in their September 7 bout.
Tyson stopped Seldon in the first round to win the WBC title.
The Lewis and Tyson camps could not agree to a deal for a bout between their two fighters. Tyson, therefore, was stripped of his title by the WBC, adhering to the court ruling.
Tyson is scheduled to put his new WBA title on the line against former undisputed champion Evander Holyfield on November 9 in Las Vegas.
If Lewis beats McCall, a Tyson-Lewis fight would be a huge money-maker.
